summary: Decompiled the keyboard cursor-movement logic for the three character-view (state 0x11) menus: the ACTION menu (EQUIP/SPELL/.../REVIEW/EXIT), the SKILL tab picker (WEAPONRY/PHYSICAL/PERSONAL/ACADEMIA/EXIT), and the SWAG menu (ADD/REMOVE/DROP/EXIT). MAJOR FINDING: ALL THREE menus call ONE shared grid navigator, ui_menu_picker_grid @ wpcvw file 0x6c. They differ ONLY in the per-menu picker arguments (msg_base, x_step, the mask, and init_cursor) -- the navigation algebra is identical across all three because it lives entirely inside 0x6c. GEOMETRY: every call passes cols(param_7)=2, which the navigator treats as the COLUMN HEIGHT (cells stacked vertically per column). The layout is COLUMN-MAJOR with 2 rows: cell index i sits at column = i div 2, row = i mod 2 (top row = even indices 0,2,4,6...; bottom row = odd indices 1,3,5...). This matches the action-menu's documented column-major 2-row layout AND is the SAME geometry for SKILL and SWAG (refuting any hypothesis that the sub-menus differ). KEY CODES (CORRECTED — see below): the navigator reads kbd-filter codes 1=LEFT, 2=UP, 3=RIGHT, 4=DOWN (NOT 0x08..0x0b), with code 5 = commit/Enter; a mouse click (*0x4fc4==1) also commits. TRANSITION RULES per NUMERIC CODE (cursor=param_9 over the ENABLED-cell count local_6=N, cols=2): code1: if (2 <= cursor) cursor-=2; code2: if (cursor%2 > 0) cursor-=1; code3: if (cursor+2 < N) cursor+=2; code4: if (cursor%2 < 1 AND cursor+1 < N) cursor+=1. ALL FOUR EDGES CLAMP (guarded if; no wrap, no column-carry). DOSBOX-VERIFIED CONCLUSION (2026-06-01, save 5 camp ACTION menu): our nextActionCursor MATCHES the engine exactly -- there is NO divergence. The subagent's initial draft transposed the code->physical-arrow labels (guessed 1=UP/2=LEFT); a live drive proved the opposite: pressing UP from EXIT(idx5) moved to SKILL(idx4) = idx-1 within-column (= code2's op, so UP=code2), and pressing LEFT from SKILL(idx4) moved to ASSAY(idx2) = idx-2 column-step (= code1's op, so LEFT=code1). Thus code1=LEFT(idx-2 column axis), code2=UP(idx-1 within column), code3=RIGHT(idx+2 column axis), code4=DOWN(idx+1 within column) -- identical to our nextActionCursor's ArrowLeft/ArrowUp/ArrowRight/ArrowDown bindings AND to our DOSBox-verified wpcmk spell picker (gridNextSchool: code1=left/2=up/3=right/4=down). On screen this is INTUITIVE (Left/Right move horizontally between columns; Up/Down move vertically within a column), NOT the transposed quirk the draft claimed. Confidence HIGH for everything: the comparators come from Ghidra's control-flow decompile (no JL/JG manual-read ambiguity), all three call sites were byte-verified, and the key mapping is now behaviorally confirmed.
method: PyGhidra DecompInterface (tools/ghidra/scripts/decompile.py, absolute project dir, GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR set, GUI closed) on ui_menu_picker_grid @ wpcvw file 0x6c -- both the C decompile and the --raw listing (the listing gives exact file offsets for every comparator since wpcvw.ovr loads at image base 0). Verified the three call sites and their cols=2 argument by (a) scanning original/wpcvw.ovr for every E8 rel16 near-call whose target == 0x6c (found 6: file 0x227b, 0x4e5c, 0x6180, 0x6793, 0x6a0b, 0x969e), and (b) reading the 0x30 bytes preceding each of the three relevant calls and decoding the right-to-left push sequence of mov ax,imm / push ax (b8 II II 50) immediates. Cross-referenced the picker args against the existing findings wpcvw-character-view-ux.json (action menu, view-input-keys), wpcvw-skill-action.json (SKILL), wpcvw-swag-action.json (SWAG), and the spell-picker axis-swap precedent in spell-picker-eligibility.json. NOTE: plain `ndisasm -b 16` linear-decode of this overlay drifts out of instruction alignment depending on the start offset (the picker prologue add sp,0xfe62 and dense LEA/IMUL sequences), so absolute offsets from raw ndisasm are unreliable here; the Ghidra control-flow listing is the authority for the comparator offsets and the push-immediate scan is the authority for the call args.

findings.claim: All three menus (ACTION, SKILL tab picker, SWAG) use ONE shared grid navigator: ui_menu_picker_grid @ wpcvw file 0x6c. There is no per-menu navigation code; the four arrow-key transitions, the commit/cancel handling, and the cursor clamp ALL live inside 0x6c. Each menu only differs in the arguments it passes (window, msg_base, mask, x_base, y_base, x_step, cols, attr, init_cursor). Exactly six call sites to 0x6c exist in the overlay (file offsets 0x227b, 0x4e5c, 0x6180, 0x6793, 0x6a0b, 0x969e); the three in scope are 0x6a0b (ACTION main menu), 0x4e5c (SKILL tabs), 0x227b (SWAG add/remove/drop). Therefore any nav fix to one menu applies to all.

evidence.details: Python scan of original/wpcvw.ovr for E8 rel16 near-calls resolving to target 0x6c yields {0x227b,0x4e5c,0x6180,0x6793,0x6a0b,0x969e}. Ghidra names the function at 0x6c ui_menu_picker_grid; its body contains the entire input loop (input_poll_key_or_mouse_with_blink(0x553e,0x3598) -> key dispatch 1/2/3/4/5 -> cursor update -> return aiStack_24[param_9]).

findings.claim: The grid is COLUMN-MAJOR with a column height (cols param_7) of 2 rows for ALL THREE menus. Cell index i is placed at screen column = (i / cols) and screen row = (i % cols): x = (i/cols)*x_step + x_base, y = (i % cols) + y_base. With cols=2 this means top row = even indices {0,2,4,6,...}, bottom row = odd indices {1,3,5,...} -- the same column-major 2-row layout the action menu was already understood to use. SKILL and SWAG are NOT a different geometry; they are byte-identical in cols. The only per-menu differences are x_step (horizontal spacing between columns: ACTION=6, SKILL=0xa, SWAG=8) and x_base/y_base (all three use x_base=2, y_base=1), none of which affect the navigation transitions.

evidence.details: Render placement in 0x6c: `iVar2 = (local_6 / param_7) * param_6 + param_4` (x, file 0x98-0xa2) and `func_0x0000bda7(param_1, iVar2, local_6 % param_7 + param_5)` (y = i%cols + y_base, file 0xa9-0xc1). param_6=x_step, param_4=x_base, param_5=y_base, param_7=cols. Per-menu cols all = 2 (see call-site findings). So column index = i/2, row index = i%2 (column-major).

findings.claim: The navigator compares the polled key against codes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 -- NOT 0x08..0x0b. Mapping (DOSBox-VERIFIED 2026-06-01, consistent with the wpcmk spell picker gridNextSchool): 1=LEFT, 2=UP, 3=RIGHT, 4=DOWN, 5=Enter/commit. A mouse click is detected separately via the global *0x4fc4==1, which forces commit (sets the local key to 5 and the cursor to the clicked cell). There is NO ESC/cancel key handling inside the navigator -- the only way out is to commit on a cell (selecting the menu's EXIT entry).

evidence.details: Raw listing (Ghidra, file offsets): 0x34d CMP AX,0x1 (UP); 0x355 CMP AX,0x2 (LEFT); 0x35d CMP AX,0x3 (DOWN); 0x365 CMP AX,0x4 (RIGHT); loop terminates `while (local_4 != 5)` so key 5 = commit. Input via input_poll_key_or_mouse_with_blink(0x553e,0x3598) -> iVar2; mouse branch at 0x226 CMP word [0x4fc4],0x1 sets local key to 5 and param_9 to clicked index.

findings.claim: LEFT (key code 1, DOSBox-verified): cursor -= cols (=2) IFF cursor >= cols. Formula: `if (cols <= cursor) cursor -= cols`. With cols=2: `if (cursor >= 2) cursor -= 2`. PHYSICAL MEANING: steps to the PREVIOUS COLUMN (the +/-2 column-major axis) = leftward on screen. CLAMP at the left/first column: when cursor < 2 (already in column 0) the key is a no-op (no wrap to the last column). Matches our nextActionCursor ArrowLeft exactly.

evidence.details: Decompile: `else if (iVar2 == 1) { if (param_7 <= param_9) { ui_grid_set_cursor_compute(...); param_9 = param_9 - param_7; } }`. Raw listing: 0x241 SUB AX,[BP+0x10] (cursor - cols); 0x244 JL 0x27a (skip move if cursor-cols < 0, i.e. require cursor >= cols); on the move path 0x277 SUB [BP+0x14],AX (param_9 -= cols). param_7=cols at [BP+0x10], param_9=cursor at [BP+0x14]. Comparator recovered by Ghidra control-flow (signed); no manual JL/JG read needed. Confidence high.

findings.claim: UP (key code 2, DOSBox-verified): cursor -= 1 IFF (cursor mod cols) > 0. Formula: `if (0 < cursor % cols) cursor -= 1`. With cols=2: `if (cursor % 2 > 0) cursor -= 1` -- i.e. only odd cursor (bottom row) moves, to the top row of the SAME column. PHYSICAL MEANING: moves UP within the 2-row column (the +/-1 row axis) = upward on screen. CLAMP on the top row: even cursor (cursor%2==0, already top row) is a no-op (no wrap to bottom, no column carry). Matches our nextActionCursor ArrowUp exactly. (DRIVE: EXIT idx5 -> SKILL idx4.)

evidence.details: Decompile: `else if (iVar2 == 2) { if (0 < param_9 % param_7) { ...; param_9 = param_9 + -1; } }`. Raw listing: 0x281 IDIV [BP+0x10] (cursor / cols, remainder in DX->AX); 0x286 CMP AX,0x0; 0x289 JLE 0x2bc (skip if remainder <= 0, i.e. require remainder > 0); decrement on the move path. Confidence high (control-flow comparator).

findings.claim: RIGHT (key code 3, DOSBox-verified): cursor += cols (=2) IFF cursor + cols < N (N = local_6 = count of ENABLED cells). Formula: `if (cursor + cols < N) cursor += cols`. With cols=2: `if (cursor + 2 < N) cursor += 2`. PHYSICAL MEANING: steps to the NEXT COLUMN (the +/-2 column-major axis) = rightward on screen. CLAMP at the right/last column: if cursor+2 >= N the key is a no-op (no wrap to first column). NOTE the bound is the enabled-cell count N, not the raw entry count -- disabled entries are excluded from the visible grid. Matches our nextActionCursor ArrowRight exactly.

evidence.details: Decompile: `else if (iVar2 == 3) { if (param_9 + param_7 < local_6) { ...; param_9 = param_9 + param_7; } }`. Raw listing: 0x2c2 ADD AX,[BP+0x10] (cursor + cols); 0x2c5 CMP AX,[BP-0x4] (vs local_6=count); 0x2c8 JGE 0x2fe (skip if cursor+cols >= count); increment on the move path 0x2fb ADD [BP+0x14],AX. local_6 (=N enabled count) at [BP-0x4]. Confidence high (control-flow comparator).

findings.claim: DOWN (key code 4, DOSBox-verified): cursor += 1 IFF (cursor mod cols) < cols-1 AND cursor+1 < N. Formula: `if (cursor % cols < cols-1 && cursor+1 < N) cursor += 1`. With cols=2: `if (cursor % 2 == 0 && cursor+1 < N) cursor += 1` -- i.e. only even cursor (top row) moves, to the bottom row of the SAME column, and only if that bottom cell exists (cursor+1 < N). PHYSICAL MEANING: moves DOWN within the 2-row column (the +/-1 row axis) = downward on screen. CLAMP on the bottom row OR when the bottom cell is past the enabled count: odd cursor, or an even cursor in the last (odd-count) column, is a no-op. Matches our nextActionCursor ArrowDown exactly.

evidence.details: Decompile: `else if (((iVar2 == 4) && (param_9 % param_7 < param_7 + -1)) && (param_9 + 1 < local_6)) { ...; param_9 = param_9 + 1; }`. Raw listing: 0x304 IDIV [BP+0x10] (cursor%cols); 0x30d CMP AX,CX (CX = cols-1 from 0x259 dec cx); 0x30f JGE 0x34b (skip if remainder >= cols-1); 0x315 CMP AX,[BP-0x4] (cursor+1 vs count); 0x318 JGE 0x34b (skip if cursor+1 >= count). Two-part guard. Confidence high (control-flow comparators).

findings.claim: EVERY edge CLAMPS; there is NO wrap-around and NO column-carry on any of the four arrows. Each handler is a guarded `if` that simply leaves the cursor unchanged when the guard fails: UP at column 0 (cursor<2) does nothing; DOWN at the last column (cursor+2>=N) does nothing; LEFT on the top row (cursor%2==0) does nothing; RIGHT on the bottom row (cursor%2>0) or when the bottom cell is past the count does nothing. So pressing UP at the top-left cell, or DOWN at the bottom-right cell, etc., is always a no-op -- the cursor never jumps to the opposite edge and never carries to an adjacent column/row across the edge. This is identical clamp behavior across ACTION, SKILL, and SWAG (one shared routine).

evidence.details: All four key branches in 0x6c are `if (<guard>) { recompute_old_cell_render; param_9 += delta; }` with no else and no fallthrough that wraps. The do/while only exits on key 5. Guards: UP `param_7<=param_9` (0x244 JL); LEFT `0<param_9%param_7` (0x289 JLE); DOWN `param_9+param_7<local_6` (0x2c8 JGE); RIGHT `param_9%param_7<param_7-1 && param_9+1<local_6` (0x30f,0x318 JGE). No wrap arithmetic anywhere.

findings.claim: The N used in the DOWN and RIGHT bounds is local_6 = the number of ENABLED cells the navigator actually rendered (it walks the mask, skipping entries whose mask word != 1, and increments local_6 only for enabled cells). param_9 (the cursor) and the returned value index into the COMPACTED enabled list (aiStack_24[param_9] maps the compacted cursor back to the original mask index). So navigation operates over the enabled-only grid: disabled menu options are not navigable cells and do not count toward N. This matters for the action menu's dynamic entry count (6 with a solo party vs 7 with 2+) and for SWAG/EDIT where options get disabled by context -- the grid shrinks and N is the post-filter count.

evidence.details: Decompile head: `local_6=0; local_4=0; while (*(int*)(param_3 + local_4*2) != -1) { if (*(int*)(param_3+local_4*2) == 1) { ...render cell local_6...; aiStack_24[local_6]=local_4; local_6++; } local_4++; }`. param_3=mask_ptr; mask terminates on -1. local_6 = enabled count = N. Return `aiStack_24[param_9]` decompacts cursor to original index. So the cursor space is the enabled subset, not raw 0..entry_count.

findings.claim: CROSS-CHECK vs our reducer's single nextActionCursor(idx,key,n): NO DIVERGENCE -- our model matches the engine exactly, both math AND arrow labels (DOSBox-verified 2026-06-01). Our model: ArrowLeft = idx-2 (col axis), ArrowRight = idx+2 (col axis), ArrowUp = idx-1 within col (idx%2==1->idx-1), ArrowDown = idx+1 within col (idx%2==0 && idx+1<n -> idx+1). The ENGINE: LEFT(code1) = idx-2, RIGHT(code3) = idx+2, UP(code2) = idx-1 within col, DOWN(code4) = idx+1 within col. With the VERIFIED code->key mapping (1=LEFT,2=UP,3=RIGHT,4=DOWN) every binding lines up: engine LEFT == our ArrowLeft, engine RIGHT == our ArrowRight, engine UP == our ArrowUp, engine DOWN == our ArrowDown. Clamp behavior, +/-2 / +/-1 magnitudes, mod-2 within-column logic, and the idx+1<n bottom-cell guard all match. On screen the navigation is intuitive (Left/Right between columns, Up/Down within a column). NO PORT CHANGE NEEDED. (An earlier draft of this finding claimed a transposed-axis divergence; that was a wrong code->key label guess, refuted by the DOSBox drive below.)

evidence.details: Engine key dispatch (file 0x34d/0x355/0x35d/0x365 = codes 1/2/3/4) bound to handlers: code1->idx-=2 (0x241/0x244), code2->idx-=1 if idx%2>0 (0x286/0x289), code3->idx+=2 if idx+2<n (0x2c5/0x2c8), code4->idx+=1 if idx%2<1 && idx+1<n (0x30d/0x315). DOSBox drive (save 5 camp ACTION menu, cursor on EXIT idx5): physical UP moved EXIT->SKILL (idx5->idx4, idx-1 within-column = code2's op, so UP=code2); physical LEFT moved SKILL->ASSAY (idx4->idx2, idx-2 column-step = code1's op, so LEFT=code1). Hence 1=LEFT,2=UP,3=RIGHT,4=DOWN, matching gridNextSchool (wpcmk spell picker) and our nextActionCursor.

transition_tables.shared_navigator: ui_menu_picker_grid @ wpcvw file 0x6c (cols=2 for all three menus). N = count of ENABLED cells. Column-major: index i -> column i/2, row i%2 (top row even, bottom row odd).

by_key_code.1_LEFT: if (idx >= 2) idx -= 2   // previous column (leftward); clamp at column 0
by_key_code.2_UP: if (idx % 2 > 0) idx -= 1   // bottom->top within column (upward); clamp on top row
by_key_code.3_RIGHT: if (idx + 2 < N) idx += 2   // next column (rightward); clamp at last column
by_key_code.4_DOWN: if (idx % 2 == 0 && idx + 1 < N) idx += 1   // top->bottom within column (downward); clamp on bottom row / missing cell
by_key_code.5_ENTER: commit; return original mask index of enabled cell idx
by_key_code.edges: ALL clamp; no wrap, no column carry
by_key_code.note: Code->key mapping 1=LEFT,2=UP,3=RIGHT,4=DOWN is DOSBox-verified; matches our nextActionCursor exactly.

per_menu_geometry.ACTION (0x6a0b): msg_base=0x12d, x_step=6, cols=2 (column-major 2-row); N = enabled action count (6 solo / 7 with REVIEW + EXIT etc., context-masked)
per_menu_geometry.SKILL (0x4e5c): msg_base=0x258, x_step=0xa, cols=2 (column-major 2-row); N = enabled category tabs + EXIT
per_menu_geometry.SWAG (0x227b): msg_base=0x2ef, x_step=8, cols=2 (column-major 2-row); N = enabled of {ADD,REMOVE,DROP} + EXIT

port_impact.current_model_status: nextActionCursor(idx,key,n) MATCHES the engine exactly for all three menus -- correct clamp, +/-2 column axis on Left/Right, +/-1 within-column axis on Up/Down (mod-2 + idx+1<n guard), and the correct arrow->axis binding (DOSBox-verified). NO FIX NEEDED.
